proof_skeleton_nl: Work in the larger weighted polynomial ring S = Q[y_1,...,y_b] with weights 1,...,b, and encode the desired construction by the ordered degree list e_i = i for i <= a and e_i = r+i for i > a. The theorem hypothesis is exactly the divisor-count condition for this list, so the bottleneck initial-interval existence theorem yields a homogeneous regular sequence u_1,...,u_b in S with those ordered degrees. The first a elements have degrees 1,...,a, so a graded triangular automorphism straightens them to the coordinate variables y_1,...,y_a. Quotienting by those variables leaves the tail as a regular sequence in S/(y_1,...,y_a), and this quotient is canonically the target ring R = Q[x_s : s in {a+1,...,b}]. The descended tail gives the family (f_s)_{s in I} with deg(f_s)=r+s in increasing order. If a=b, the tail is empty, so the witness family is the empty family.

steps.derives: Define S := Q[y_1,...,y_b] with weighted grading deg(y_i)=i for 1 <= i <= b. Define the ordered list e_1,...,e_b by e_i = i for 1 <= i <= a and e_i = r+i for a < i <= b. Also define I := {a+1,...,b} and R := Q[x_s : s in I] with deg(x_s)=s.
steps.trivial_justification: This is only the setup of the larger ring, the ordered degree list, and the target ring.

steps.derives: For every positive integer d, the ordered list e_1,...,e_b satisfies |{i in {1,...,b} : d divides e_i}| >= |{i in {1,...,b} : d divides i}|.
steps.trivial_justification: Apply L1 directly to the theorem hypothesis M_d(r+a, r+b) >= M_d(a,b) for all positive d. This converts the interval count assumption into the divisor-count condition required in the enlarged ring S.

steps.derives: There exist homogeneous polynomials u_1,...,u_b in S such that deg(u_i)=e_i for each i and the ordered list u_1,...,u_b is a regular sequence in S.
steps.trivial_justification: Invoke L2 with the nonnegative integer b, the ordered positive degree list e_1,...,e_b from A1, and the divisor-count inequalities proved in A2.

steps.derives: The prefix u_1,...,u_a is a homogeneous regular sequence in S, and deg(u_i)=i for each i=1,...,a.
steps.trivial_justification: A prefix of a regular sequence is regular by the definition of regular sequence, and by A3 the first a degrees are exactly e_i=i.

steps.derives: There exists a graded Q-algebra automorphism phi : S -> S such that phi(u_i)=y_i for every i=1,...,a.
steps.trivial_justification: Apply L3 to the homogeneous regular prefix u_1,...,u_a of degrees 1,...,a obtained in A4.

steps.derives: The ordered list y_1,...,y_a, phi(u_{a+1}),...,phi(u_b) is a homogeneous regular sequence in S. Moreover, for each s in I = {a+1,...,b}, one has deg(phi(u_s)) = deg(u_s) = r+s.
steps.trivial_justification: Apply L4 to the full homogeneous regular sequence u_1,...,u_b from A3 and the graded automorphism phi from A5. Because phi(u_i)=y_i for i <= a and degrees are preserved under phi, the transformed full sequence has the stated form and degrees.

steps.derives: In the quotient ring S/(y_1,...,y_a), the images of phi(u_{a+1}),...,phi(u_b) form a homogeneous regular sequence. For each s in I, the image of phi(u_s) has weighted degree r+s.
steps.trivial_justification: Use L5 with prefix y_1,...,y_a and tail phi(u_{a+1}),...,phi(u_b) from A6. The lemma says the tail remains regular after quotienting by the prefix, and the graded version preserves homogeneity and degrees.

steps.derives: Via the canonical graded Q-algebra isomorphism S/(y_1,...,y_a) ≅ R from L6, define for each s in I the element f_s in R to be the image of the class of phi(u_s). Then each f_s is homogeneous of degree r+s, and the ordered list (f_s) for s=a+1,a+2,...,b is a regular sequence in R.
steps.trivial_justification: Apply L6 to identify the quotient from A7 with the target ring R from A1. Because L6 preserves homogeneous regular sequences and degrees under this graded isomorphism, the descended tail gives the desired ordered regular sequence in R.

steps.derives: There exists a family (f_s) indexed by I = {a+1,...,b} of homogeneous polynomials in R such that deg(f_s)=r+s for every s in I, and the ordered list of these polynomials in increasing s is a regular sequence in R. If a=b, then I is empty and the family is empty. This is exactly the root theorem statement.
steps.trivial_justification: A8 already constructs the required family with the correct indexing, degrees, and regularity. When a=b there is no tail, so the resulting family is the empty family in R=Q, exactly as required.
